meaning.en: To write something on someone else's behalf, usually a speech or article that is passed off as theirs.
meaning.zh: 替别人写文章或讲话稿，由别人署名。

examples.zh: 这本回忆录是他请人捉刀代笔的。
examples.en: This memoir was ghostwritten for him.

examples.zh: 领导的发言稿一向由秘书捉刀代笔。
examples.en: The boss's speeches are always drafted by his secretary.

examples.zh: 论文不能找人捉刀代笔，否则算作弊。
examples.en: You can't have someone write your thesis for you; that counts as cheating.

story.en: Cao Cao, feeling unimpressive in appearance, had a handsome officer receive an envoy while he stood by holding a sword as a guard; the envoy still saw through it. 'Holding the sword' came to mean standing in for someone, then writing for them.
story.zh: 魏武帝自以为形貌丑陋，让崔季珪代为接见匈奴使者，自己握刀立于床头。后来“捉刀”指代人做事，尤指代人写作。

usage.en: Verb phrase, neutral to slightly critical. The 'knife' is a sword, not a pen: the 捉刀 part comes from a story about a stand-in guard.
usage.zh: 作谓语，中性略带贬义。“刀”指佩刀，“捉刀”源自替人站岗的故事。

meaning.en: To make a tangle worse by trying to sort it out the wrong way, so that a problem grows more confused.
meaning.zh: 整理乱丝反而越理越乱，比喻做事方法不对，使问题更加复杂。

examples.zh: 他想用谎话掩盖错误，结果治丝益棼。
examples.en: He tried to cover up his mistake with lies and only made the mess worse.

examples.zh: 方案改来改去，反而治丝益棼，团队更糊涂了。
examples.en: The plan was revised again and again, only deepening the confusion.

examples.zh: 对旧制度的零敲碎打，只会治丝益棼。
examples.en: Piecemeal tinkering with the old system will only add to the muddle.

story.en: Zhongzhong said Zhouxu's rebellion was like 'sorting silk threads yet tangling them further' (犹治丝而棼之也).

usage.en: Predicate; derogatory, formal or written. 棼 is read fén (tangled), not fēn.
usage.zh: 作谓语，含贬义，多用于书面。“棼”读fén，意为纷乱。

meaning.en: To fan your parents' pillow in summer and warm their quilt in winter; to care for them attentively.
meaning.zh: 夏天为父母扇凉枕席，冬天为父母暖被，形容子女孝顺、照顾周到。

examples.zh: 他远离家乡，无法扇枕温衾，心中常感愧疚。
examples.en: Far from home, he cannot look after his parents day to day and often feels guilty.

examples.zh: 古人讲究晨昏定省、扇枕温衾，以尽孝道。
examples.en: The ancients stressed daily greetings and tending to parents' comfort as filial duty.

examples.zh: 她辞去工作回乡，只为在父母身边扇枕温衾。
examples.en: She quit her job and went home just to look after her parents.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; literary, praising filial piety. Used with 黄香 as the classic exemplar.
usage.zh: 作谓语、定语，书面语，多赞孝行；典型人物是东汉黄香。

natural: work only for someone else's benefit

meaning.en: To do hard work only for the benefit of others, getting nothing for yourself.
meaning.zh: 为别人做嫁衣，比喻白白辛苦，让别人得到好处。

equivalents: do all the work for someone else's gain

examples.zh: 我们辛苦研发，结果只是为人作嫁。
examples.en: We worked hard on development and ended up doing it for someone else.

examples.zh: 代工厂利润微薄，常有为人作嫁的感叹。
examples.en: Contract manufacturers earn little and often feel they are working for others.

examples.zh: 别总为人作嫁，也要为自己打算。
examples.en: Don't keep working for others' benefit; think of yourself too.

story.en: A poor girl who can embroider fine gold thread laments: 'Year after year I press gold thread, making wedding clothes for others' (苦恨年年压金线，为他人作嫁衣裳).
story.zh: 唐诗：“苦恨年年压金线，为他人作嫁衣裳。”

usage.en: Predicate; slightly rueful. The original 'wedding dress' image is of a poor seamstress.
usage.zh: 作谓语，带无奈、惋惜的语气。原诗写贫女为别人做嫁衣。

meaning.en: Mountains calling and the sea roaring: describes a huge, thundering noise, or a great force or crowd in motion.
meaning.zh: 像山在呼喊、海在咆哮，形容声势浩大，场面壮观。

examples.zh: 球进了，体育场里顿时山呼海啸。
examples.en: When the ball went in, the stadium erupted in a thunderous roar.

examples.zh: 台风登陆时山呼海啸，令人胆寒。
examples.en: As the typhoon landed, it roared like mountains and sea, chilling to hear.

examples.zh: 改革的浪潮山呼海啸般涌来。
examples.en: The tide of reform came surging in with tremendous force.

usage.en: Attributive or predicate; vivid, written. Not necessarily bad: it can be awe-inspiring or exciting.
usage.zh: 作定语、谓语，形象生动，多用于书面；不一定贬义，可表壮观。

meaning.en: To fling out one's sleeve and spring up, resolved to act; to take decisive action in anger or determination.
meaning.zh: 甩袖而起，形容下定决心，立刻行动。

examples.zh: 听说同胞受难，他投袂而起，立即赶赴灾区。
examples.en: Hearing of his compatriots' suffering, he sprang into action and rushed to the disaster zone.

examples.zh: 面对不公，她投袂而起，为村民讨说法。
examples.en: Faced with injustice, she rose up to seek redress for the villagers.

examples.zh: 全队投袂而起，誓要夺回冠军。
examples.en: The whole team rose resolutely, determined to win back the title.

story.en: On hearing that his envoy had been killed in Song, King Zhuang of Chu flung out his sleeve and rose up (楚子闻之，投袂而起).

usage.en: Predicate; literary, positive. 袂 (mèi) means sleeve.
usage.zh: 作谓语，书面语，含褒义。“袂”读mèi，指衣袖。

meaning.en: Remaining the same as before, unchanged despite circumstances or advice; often implies stubbornness.
meaning.zh: 仍然是老样子，没有改变。

examples.zh: 批评了多次，他依然故我。
examples.en: He has been criticised many times but carries on just as before.

examples.zh: 名满天下后，她依然故我，生活简朴。
examples.en: Even after becoming famous, she remained her old self and lived simply.

examples.zh: 城市日新月异，这家老店却依然故我。
examples.en: The city changes daily, yet this old shop stays just as it was.

usage.en: Predicate; neutral, but with critical tone when about faults and praise when about staying humble. Always refers to a person's manner.
usage.zh: 作谓语，中性；用于缺点时含贬义，用于保持本色时含褒义。

meaning.en: To treat others with complete sincerity and loyalty, as if one's liver and gall were laid open to view.
meaning.zh: 以真心诚意待人，坦诚忠诚。

examples.zh: 他为人肝胆照人，朋友遍天下。
examples.en: He is utterly sincere with others and has friends everywhere.

examples.zh: 两位老友肝胆照人，从不猜疑。
examples.en: The two old friends are completely open with each other and never doubt.

examples.zh: 她对待同事肝胆照人，赢得大家信任。
examples.en: She is wholeheartedly sincere towards colleagues and has won everyone's trust.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; commendatory. Liver and gall stand for courage and true feeling.
usage.zh: 作谓语、定语，含褒义。肝胆比喻勇气和真情。

meaning.en: So pressed by urgency that there is no time to choose carefully; taking whatever is at hand.
meaning.zh: 情况紧急，来不及选择。

examples.zh: 要赶火车，他急不暇择，随手抓了件外套就跑。
examples.en: Rushing for the train, he grabbed whatever coat was at hand and ran.

examples.zh: 资金链断裂，公司急不暇择，接受了苛刻条件。
examples.en: With funding drying up, the firm had no choice but to accept harsh terms.

examples.zh: 急不暇择之下，她选了第一家租房中介。
examples.en: In a rush, she chose the first rental agent she found.

usage.en: Predicate; written. Often used for hurried, unsatisfactory choices.
usage.zh: 作谓语，多用于书面，常指仓促而不理想的选择。

meaning.en: Educated and understanding of proper conduct; cultured and reasonable.
meaning.zh: 有文化修养，懂得道理，通情达理。

examples.zh: 她知书达理，待人接物很有分寸。
examples.en: She is cultured and courteous, and handles people with tact.

examples.zh: 这位知书达理的老师深受学生爱戴。
examples.en: This well-bred, well-read teacher is much loved by her students.

examples.zh: 他出身书香门第，从小知书达理。
examples.en: Born into a scholarly family, he has been well-read and mannered since childhood.

usage.en: Mostly attributive or predicate, often used for women or the young; commendatory. Also written 知书达礼.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语，常用于称赞女子或晚辈，含褒义；也作“知书达礼”。

meaning.en: Eyes wide open and glaring in fury.
meaning.zh: 愤怒地瞪大眼睛。

examples.zh: 他怒目圆睁，指着对方大喝一声。
examples.en: He glared furiously and shouted at the other man, pointing.

examples.zh: 门神怒目圆睁，威风凛凛。
examples.en: The door god glares with wide eyes, fearsome and majestic.

examples.zh: 听到这个消息，老板怒目圆睁，拍案而起。
examples.en: On hearing the news, the boss glared in rage and slammed the table.

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial; descriptive. Common in fiction and narrative.
usage.zh: 作谓语、状语，多用于叙事描写。

meaning.en: Writing that reads smoothly, with fitting words and clear structure.
meaning.zh: 文章通顺，用词妥帖。

examples.zh: 这篇作文文从字顺，条理清楚。
examples.en: This essay is fluent and clearly organised.

examples.zh: 修改后的稿子文从字顺，读起来舒服多了。
examples.en: The revised draft reads smoothly and is far more pleasant.

examples.zh: 翻译要做到文从字顺，不能生硬。
examples.en: A translation should be fluent, not stilted.

origin.source: 韩愈《南阳樊绍述墓志铭》

story.en: Han Yu praises Fan Shaoshu's prose: 'each word in its proper place, the writing flowing' (文从字顺各识职).
story.zh: 韩愈称赞樊绍述的文章：“文从字顺各识职。”

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; praise of writing quality. Commonly used in school and editing contexts.
usage.zh: 作谓语、定语，称赞文章通顺，常见于教学与编辑场合。

natural: rush to help others in trouble

meaning.en: To be eager to help others in their difficulties.
meaning.zh: 热心帮助别人解决困难。

examples.zh: 他急人之难，邻居有事总找他。
examples.en: He rushes to help in trouble, so neighbours always turn to him.

examples.zh: 这位企业家急人之难，捐款无数。
examples.en: This entrepreneur has donated generously, always ready to help those in need.

examples.zh: 朋友遇到麻烦，她总是急人之难。
examples.en: When friends are in trouble, she is always first to help.

usage.en: Predicate; commendatory. Often paired with 乐善好施.
usage.zh: 作谓语，含褒义，常与“乐善好施”连用。

meaning.en: A person's former students and old friends; the network of connections built up over a career.
meaning.zh: 门下的学生和旧友，泛指关系网。

examples.zh: 他的门生故旧遍布政界和学界。
examples.en: His former students and old friends are everywhere in politics and academia.

examples.zh: 寿宴上，门生故旧齐聚一堂。
examples.en: At the birthday banquet, his protégés and old friends all gathered.

examples.zh: 门生故旧的举荐帮了他不少忙。
examples.en: Recommendations from his protégés and old acquaintances helped him a lot.

usage.en: Noun phrase; neutral, but can imply cronyism in discussions of patronage.
usage.zh: 名词性，中性；谈论人情关系时可带结党的意味。

meaning.en: Even a skilled person or favourite can suffer an unexpected failure through carelessness.
meaning.zh: 比喻有经验的人或强者因疏忽而遭遇意外失败。

examples.zh: 夺冠热门在半决赛马失前蹄，让人意外。
examples.en: The title favourite came a cropper in the semi-final, a big surprise.

examples.zh: 他做事一向稳妥，这次竟然马失前蹄。
examples.en: He is normally careful, yet this time he slipped up.

examples.zh: 再有经验也要小心，免得马失前蹄。
examples.en: Even the experienced must be careful lest they stumble.

usage.en: Predicate; often used of sports or business upsets. Neutral to sympathetic, often as a warning.
usage.zh: 作谓语，多用于比赛、事业中的意外失利，常带警示意味。

synonyms: 阴沟里翻船——没想到的事

natural: calamity that wipes out a whole family

meaning.en: A disaster in which an entire family is killed or destroyed.
meaning.zh: 全家被杀害或毁灭的灾祸。

equivalents: the destruction of a whole family

examples.zh: 一场仇杀，给这个家族带来了灭门之祸。
examples.en: A vendetta brought the whole family to destruction.

examples.zh: 他得罪了权贵，招来灭门之祸。
examples.en: He offended the powerful and brought disaster on his entire family.

examples.zh: 影片讲述一家人遭遇灭门之祸后的复仇。
examples.en: The film tells of a family's revenge after its near-annihilation.

usage.en: Noun phrase; used of history and crime stories. Also 灭门惨案 in news.
usage.zh: 名词性，多用于历史和案件叙事；新闻中也说“灭门惨案”。

meaning.en: Young men from noble or wealthy families, usually pampered.
meaning.zh: 旧时指贵族或富家子弟。

examples.zh: 宴席上坐满了王孙公子。
examples.en: The banquet was filled with noble scions.

examples.zh: 他虽是王孙公子，却不爱奢华。
examples.en: Though a nobleman's son, he disliked extravagance.

examples.zh: 小说描写了王孙公子的浮华生活。
examples.en: The novel depicts the showy life of aristocratic young men.

usage.en: Noun phrase; literary, can be slightly mocking. Mainly historical.
usage.zh: 名词性，书面语，略带讽刺，多指旧时。

meaning.en: A famous reputation is fully earned; the real thing lives up to its name.
meaning.zh: 名声与实际相符，没有虚假。

examples.zh: 亲眼见他演奏，才知道名下无虚。
examples.en: Seeing him play in person, I knew his fame was well deserved.

examples.zh: 这家老字号果然名下无虚。
examples.en: This old brand really lives up to its name.

examples.zh: 大师的作品名下无虚，令人折服。
examples.en: The master's works justify his fame and are truly convincing.

usage.en: Predicate; formal, praise. Often follows 果然.
usage.zh: 作谓语，褒义，较书面，常与“果然”连用。

meaning.en: A family of high social standing and prestige.
meaning.zh: 有名望、有地位的家族。

examples.zh: 她出身名门望族，家教极好。
examples.en: She comes from a distinguished family and was brought up well.

examples.zh: 这座古宅曾属一户名门望族。
examples.en: This old house once belonged to a prominent family.

examples.zh: 小说主人公是江南的名门望族之后。
examples.en: The protagonist descends from a prominent family of the Jiangnan region.

usage.en: Noun phrase; mostly commendatory.
usage.zh: 名词性，多含褒义。

meaning.en: Features as fine as a painting; elegantly handsome or beautiful.
meaning.zh: 眉眼清秀，像画出来的一样。

examples.zh: 画中少女眉目如画，令人难忘。
examples.en: The girl in the painting has picture-perfect features and is unforgettable.

examples.zh: 他眉目如画，是学校里的美男子。
examples.en: With his fine features, he is the handsome boy of the school.

examples.zh: 这位女演员眉目如画，气质出众。
examples.en: The actress has finely drawn features and exceptional poise.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; praise of looks. Used for both genders.
usage.zh: 作谓语、定语，称赞容貌，男女皆可用。

meaning.en: People who, frustrated, make trouble and break the law; ruffians.
meaning.zh: 因不得志而为非作歹的人。

examples.zh: 几个不逞之徒在街上寻衅滋事。
examples.en: A few thugs were picking fights on the street.

examples.zh: 警方抓获了一批不逞之徒。
examples.en: The police arrested a group of ruffians.

examples.zh: 别和这些不逞之徒来往。
examples.en: Don't hang about with these louts.

usage.en: Noun phrase; derogatory. 逞 here means 'be satisfied/have one's way'.
usage.zh: 名词性，含贬义。“逞”意为称心、得志。

meaning.en: Regret that comes too late to change anything.
meaning.zh: 后悔也来不及了。

equivalents: rue it when it's too late

examples.zh: 早不努力，现在悔之无及。
examples.en: He didn't work hard earlier and now it is too late for regrets.

examples.zh: 轻信骗子，等到被骗光积蓄才悔之无及。
examples.en: He trusted the swindler and regretted it only after losing his savings.

examples.zh: 现在不保护环境，将来必然悔之无及。
examples.en: If we don't protect the environment now, we will surely regret it too late.

usage.en: Predicate; often in warnings. Also 悔之不及.
usage.zh: 作谓语，常用于警示；也作“悔之不及”。

meaning.en: The insight to judge people's character and ability correctly.
meaning.zh: 能识别人才、了解人的见识。

examples.zh: 老板很有知人之明，选的人都很合适。
examples.en: The boss has a good eye for talent; everyone he picks is a good fit.

examples.zh: 没有知人之明，就难以选好接班人。
examples.en: Without good judgement of people, it's hard to choose a successor.

examples.zh: 她缺乏知人之明，屡次被朋友欺骗。
examples.en: She lacks judgement of character and is repeatedly cheated by friends.

usage.en: Noun phrase, often 有/缺乏知人之明; typically used about leaders. Often paired with 自知之明.
usage.zh: 名词性，常作“有/缺乏知人之明”，多指领导者；常与“自知之明”对举。

meaning.en: To lift one's head and wait expectantly; to look forward to something eagerly.
meaning.zh: 抬起头来盼望等待，形容殷切期待。

examples.zh: 球迷们翘首以待新赛季开始。
examples.en: Fans are eagerly waiting for the new season.

examples.zh: 全家人翘首以待他的归来。
examples.en: The whole family is eagerly awaiting his return.

examples.zh: 新书上市前，读者已翘首以待。
examples.en: Before the book came out, readers were already looking forward to it.

usage.en: Predicate; 翘 reads qiáo here (not qiào). Common in news and announcements.
usage.zh: 作谓语，“翘”读qiáo；常见于新闻和公告。
